correctness.rationale: Step 1 proves the hemispherical intersection is exactly the graph because a mixed edge must be an original cross edge and no same-side edge lies in both covers. Step 2 explicitly collapses each cone relative to its nonempty base, leaving whole part simplices under opposite-side universal vertices. Step 3 invokes the homotopy-pushout theorem and the integral Mayer–Vietoris isomorphism. The n>=4 crown boundary-sphere endpoint is separated from j>=1, and the first map is compared by naturality of the MV sequence; at n=4 the two lost degree-two generators and one new generator are accounted for. For later steps graph edge insertion injects cycle homology with primitive rank-one cokernel. verify.py independently enumerates 26 crown stages and 64 random universal-pair graphs, checks 8352 free-face pairs and nine inclusion ranks, supplementing rather than proving the infinite claim.

originality.rationale: The exact crown endpoint is already classified by two published open-neighborhood prism theorems, and is explicitly credited as old. Their facet descriptions show equivalence to the closed-neighborhood crown endpoint; this is a strong implication comparison, not a mere title comparison. Their coverage stops before any deleted matching pair is restored and contains no degree-two inclusion-map statement. The first restoration supplies a genuine change of topology and a natural persistence law for every further restoration. Matsushita’s full available 2025 treatment defines closed neighborhoods and relates their fundamental groups to graph path groups, but does not prove this universal-pair suspension or the specific integral persistence maps. Dense bipartite restored crowns contain K2,3, so the separate published triangle-free/K2,3-free closed-neighborhood normal form does not apply. Related prior crown-graph findings about two-independence complexes concern a different invariant and do not imply the claimed homotopy types. Searches and inspections reduce but cannot eliminate priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The result identifies a sharp, natural topology-changing edge insertion in a one-parameter filtration starting at a previously studied, nontrivial mixed-dimensional wedge. The universal-pair criterion upgrades a graph cycle-space invariant to integral second-homology by a constructive two-hemisphere model across a broad graph class, and the restoration filtration makes exact predictions for homotopy types and all integral degree-two persistence maps. At n=4 the first inclusion has two independent dying classes and one new birth; for n>=5 two higher-dimensional classes die while the later sequence has primitive rank-one births. These features are motivated by the known crown endpoint rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
